elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap is expressed per-Party and therefore binds Vendor and Customer alike.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; the alternative USD 1,000,000 floor and the "greater of" construction are absent.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7(a): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES" — mutual by its terms and left unchanged.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted carve-out: "Except with respect to a Party's indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or wilful misconduct..." — confidentiality breach sits outside the cap for both Parties.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list omits data protection and security obligations; such breaches would fall inside the 12-month fees cap. Drafter must add "breach of its data protection or security obligations" to the carve-out list.
Inserted carve-out expressly excepts "a Party's indemnification obligations" from the cap; consistent with the retained 7(a) exception for indemnification.
No reference to fraud anywhere in the operative language; add "fraud" to the cap carve-out list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out; add "infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights" to the exception clause.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap contains no statement that Customer's obligation to pay fees due is outside the cap; as drafted Customer's payment obligations could be argued to sit inside the 12-month fees cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetrical, no one-sided protection of Vendor and no retained unlimited-Customer-liability language.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fees basis; "paid or payable" is broader than "paid" and favourable to Customer, and no narrow defined "Fees" term limits it.
"Except with respect to a Party's indemnification obligations ... aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" — indemnities sit above the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "breach of confidentiality obligations" appears in the exception list preceding the cap.
"gross negligence" expressly listed in the cap exception.
"wilful misconduct" expressly listed in the cap exception.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original Section 7 contains only a mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no aggregate cap anywhere in the Agreement, so both parties' direct exposure was unlimited — a material failure of the fallback's mutual 12-month-fees cap.

The redline is position-complete at the fallback level: all six fallback elements (mutual cap, 12-month fees basis, and uncapped indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct) are satisfied in the single inserted sentence.

Preferred level is not reached: the USD 1,000,000 alternative floor / "greater of" formulation, and the data protection & security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs are absent, as is the statement that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to the cap. To reach preferred, amend to "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" and extend the exception list to data protection/security obligations, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, plus a sentence that Customer's obligation to pay fees due is not subject to the cap.

Minimal: one concise sentence added to a section that lacked a cap entirely; existing favourable language (the mutual consequential-damages exclusion with its indemnification and confidentiality exceptions) is retained verbatim, nothing outside the checklist is deleted, and no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories are bolted on.

Preserves intent: the new cap sits alongside, and does not contradict, the retained 7(a) exclusion (the same indemnification and confidentiality items are excepted in both), no defined term is left dangling, and the fees, warranty and indemnity mechanics are untouched.

Drafting nit (rationale-level, not a defect): the temporal anchor is "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" rather than the preferred "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — acceptable at fallback but worth aligning if the preferred formula is pursued.
